lines.x: Ryanair reported a 15% drop in first-half profit and warned of a €2 billion higher fuel bill for next year.
European stock indices closed lower on Friday, with Ireland's Iseq All-Share falling 0.73%, as broader European equity markets decoupled from temporary rebounds in US tech shares.
Ryanair is considering pay freezes, crew reductions, and increased use of AI as cost-cutting measures to offset soaring fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict, risking clashes with unions.
Shares of Irish nutrition company Glanbia fell 6% after Morgan Stanley lowered its rating on the stock to underweight.
